description: chain_walk (lib.rs:2109): the fold used to detect whether any parent matched and simultaneously push new_nodes has a logic smell: 'fold(false, |_, _parent| { new_nodes.push(...); true })'. The closure ignores the accumulator '_ ' and always returns true — which means matched_via_i is true iff ANY parent matched (at least one iteration ran), and the push always fires. This is equivalent to: 'let matched_via_i = tree.iter().filter(...).fold(false, |acc, parent| { new_nodes.push(...); true });'. The discard of acc is correct (we only care about whether at least one match fired), but the idiom of fold with discarded accumulator is unusual and confusing. Replace with: 'let matched_via_i = tree.iter().filter(...).count() > 0; for _ in tree.iter().filter(...) { new_nodes.push(...); }' or use .inspect() + .count() for clarity.
title: pkix-path: matched_via_i fold closure discards accumulator, returning only last value
